newsitem.title: INDIA: Political uproar knocks Bombay shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Political uproar knocks Bombay shares at close.

text.p: Bombay stocks fell victim to political concerns on Thursday due to divisions in the ruling coalition over its association with a break-away faction of Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav, traders said.
After market hours, the Patna High Court said it had rejected Yadav's appeal for "anticipatory bail" to avert arrest by federal police in a corruption scandal.
"Rumours of the arrest of Laloo Prasad Yadav took a toll on the market," said Vidyut Devendra Kumar, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange.

The Bihar chief minister, who earlier this month broke away from Indian premier Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, has refused to resign after federal police indicted him in a $280 million corruption case in which he says he is innocent.
Dealers said heavy selling pressure near close on the penultimate day of weekly trade indicated a nervous undertone.

"For most of the trading session, the market traded in a narrow band and lacked direction," SBI Capital Markets said in a commentary. "Fund support...was lacking which led to the market crash near the end. We expect the market to weaken futher."
Among individual shares, Housing Development Finance Company (HDFC) surged seven percent to 4,145.0 rupees after the firm announced a rise in its first quarter net profit.
But profit-taking arrested the sharp rise and the stock closed with a net gain of 63.50 rupees at 3,940.0 rupees.
HDFC said its profit after tax rose to 549.1 million rupees for the three months ended June 30 from 427.2 million rupees in the year-ago period.
Shares of India's leading shoe-maker Bata India rose 6.0 rupees, or 4 pct to a record 150.0 after it posted impressive six-month results in the six months ending June 30, 1997.
